headline: Build and test your Asana integration instantly with optional App Directory review taking around one week.
summary: Asana offers a developer-friendly OAuth 2.0 API with instant access to testing and own-workspace distribution without review. Standalone external integrations are self-serve, while listing in the public App Directory or using native App Components requires a formal security and QA review.
approval_wait: None for private/unlisted use; ~1 week for App Directory
time_to_production: Instant for own workspace; 1 week for public directory

oauth.pkce: Supported using code_challenge and code_challenge_method=S256 (or plain)
oauth.refresh_tokens: Supported; returned with the initial token exchange, long-lived with no fixed expiration window, valid until explicitly revoked.
oauth.redirect_uri_rules: Must strictly match registered URLs. Non-native web apps require secure https://. Native/CLI apps can use urn:ietf:wg:oauth:2.0:oob.
oauth.scopes: Required scopes must be explicitly enabled in the Developer Console under OAuth > Permission scopes before authorization.

steps.title: Register the application
steps.detail: Create a new app in the Developer Console under 'My apps', configure the app name, and generate the client_id and client_secret.

steps.title: Configure OAuth scopes and redirect URIs
steps.detail: Set up HTTPS redirect URIs and enable standard scopes (projects:read, tasks:read, tasks:write, users:read) in the Developer Console.

steps.title: Test OAuth flow
steps.detail: Execute the authorization code flow with PKCE and the state parameter using a workspace you are a member of.

steps.title: Set workspace distribution
steps.detail: Select 'Specific workspaces' to distribute to your own org, or select 'Any workspace' for multi-tenant unlisted distribution.

steps.title: Draft app directory profile
steps.detail: Prepare an app listing profile with a unique icon, screenshots, a short summary, and a long description of at least 250 characters.

steps.title: Provide legal and demo assets
steps.detail: Supply verified company info, privacy policy URL, support URL, step-by-step instructions, and a screencast video.

steps.title: Wait for QA and Security Review
steps.detail: Asana reviews the submission to ensure no trademark infringements, correct CSRF state validation, and working flow.

requirements.text: App listing requires a long description of at least 250 characters without formatting or grammatical errors.
Submission must include a direct URL to a publicly accessible Privacy Policy.
OAuth implementation must use a secure HTTPS redirect URL and implement CSRF prevention via an unguessable state parameter.
Review submission demands a screencast video demonstrating the app and step-by-step setup instructions.

gotchas.text: Using native Asana terms (tasks, projects, workflows, automations) in UI labels or dropdowns can cause app rejection.
There are conflicting statements in the documentation regarding whether multi-tenant ('Any workspace') distribution via a direct link requires formal review.
Missing or improperly validated CSRF state parameters frequently trigger rejection during security QA.
Rate limits apply per authorization token (per user). Free tier domains are limited to 150 requests per minute; Paid tier domains are limited to 1,500.
Requesting an OAuth scope during authorization that hasn't been explicitly enabled in the Developer Console yields a 'forbidden_scopes' error.

permissions.review_impact: Standard resource scope. No elevated verification or paid tier required. Admin consent is not required by default.

permissions.action: Create tasks and update task status & properties

blockers.issue: API requests return HTTP 429 Too Many Requests.
blockers.how_to_proceed: Parse the 'Retry-After' header in the response and pause the agent's requests for the indicated number of seconds before retrying.
Log into the Developer Console, navigate to 'OAuth > Permission scopes', and explicitly enable the requested scopes.

blockers.issue: App Directory submission rejected for text or vocabulary failures.
blockers.how_to_proceed: Rewrite the app description to exceed 250 characters, remove Asana-specific terminology (like 'tasks' or 'projects') from your UI, and fix any typographical errors.

agent_can: Configure the OAuth authorization URL with PKCE and the state parameter
Test the token exchange and API endpoints within an approved workspace
Draft the minimum 250-character app description and privacy policy text
Handle HTTP 429 rate limit responses by backing off based on the Retry-After header
you_must: Register the application in the Asana Developer Console to retrieve the client_id and client_secret
Provide verified company information and host the privacy policy on a public URL
Record and upload a screencast video demonstrating the app for directory review
Ensure your Asana account has access to the workspace(s) you wish to test with

key_claims.text: The Asana authorization endpoint (https://app.asana.com/-/oauth_authorize) is active and reachable.
Asana's OAuth flow supports PKCE with the S256 challenge method.
No payment or partner program enrollment is required to build or distribute an OAuth app.
Initial response time for app review submissions is roughly one week.

open_questions: Does choosing 'Any workspace' for unlisted distribution truly allow external access without a formal app review, given the conflicting statements in the documentation?
